hi Brad,
 I can't really say whether your solution is reasonable or not, but if you're counting individual groups and worried about group size, then I think a more complex hierarchical model could be developed, mostly likely in one of the BUGS engines -- group size being an individual level covariate in this case.  Alternatively, you could stratify by group size - maybe something like small/medium/large, and treat them as having different p's or something like that.
 Maybe some other people on the unmarked list have ideas about group size they can share.
regards,
andy

Subject: [unmarked] Group Size and Abundance Covariates

Hi All,
 

My topic searches have been fruitless, on an issue that I'm sure is not a new one.

I’m conducting surveys of whooping cranes (large white birds) in an open coastal environment, where I assume I can accurately tell group size.  Using the plotted locations of groups we have used CDS to obtain abundance estimates (predicted number of groups X average group size), with arguably an unacceptable level of precision (CV ~20%).  My initial application of spatial distance sampling has improved our precision markedly by using habitat covariates to predict abundance.  In doing so, I have run into a small dilemma.  There is a behavioral response of whooping cranes that results in different group sizes dependent upon the vegetation community they occupy.  For example, while in marsh the group size typically ranges 1-4, however, while they exploit resources in burned uplands the group size can be 20+.  In the current analyses all groups are being treated similarly regardless of their size.  In all prior CDS analyses there was no indication of size-biased detection, but I am concerned that group size is not being appropriately considered when modeling abundance.  One potential work-around may be to replicate the records for each group based upon its size and essentially model locations of individuals.  Is this an appropriate solution?  Would the variance estimates for density/abundance still be defensible or biased low?  Any suggestions are appreciated.
